questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “Achilles' heel”:
questions.why: Achilles' heel is a weak spot in an otherwise strong person. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “verbose”:
questions.why: 'Verbose' means using too many words; 'succinct' means briefly expressed. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: “Seldom ____ such a rare disease been reported in this district.”
questions.why: Seldom + has + singular subject + past participle (present perfect passive). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “meticulous”:
questions.why: Meticulous = showing great attention to detail. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “Bread and butter are his daily breakfast.”
questions.why: Two nouns that name one thing take a singular verb: 'is'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “I will come tomorrow.”
opts: He said that I would come the next day.
He said that he would come the next day.
He said that he would come yesterday.
He said that he will come tomorrow.
questions.why: will → would; tomorrow → the next day. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “He looks pale; he ______ be unwell.”
questions.why: 'Must' for a confident deduction. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “It was the first time she ____ a surgery on her own.”
questions.why: 'It was the first time' takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “benign”:
questions.why: 'Benign' means gentle or harmless; 'malignant' means harmful or evil in intent. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “No sooner had he reached the station when the train left.”
questions.why: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than', not 'when'. GPSC-style practice item.
